title: Nathan Hawkins vs Joe Folley: Free Will, Compatibilism, and Idealism
label: Free will, agency, and idealism
motion: Can libertarian free will and Bradleyan idealism answer determinist and naturalist pressure better than compatibilist pragmatism?
sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 983dfe6da87ddc08124eec2f136b7822b786e544d8bdb6d961eb477cd770bcfa). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.
summary: Hawkins defended libertarian idealism through normativity and experiential completeness, while Folley’s modal distinctions and disciplined pragmatism applied stronger comparative pressure.

pro.text: those logical principles set the standards for how you ought to think
pro.context: Hawkins uses objective logical relations to distinguish norm-governed inference from the merely descriptive psychology of how people happen to reason.

con.text: otherwise is being used with two really different scopes
con.context: Folley identifies the central modal mismatch between broadly varying possible worlds and alternatives that preserve the actual past and laws.

pro.words: The reversibility of time-symmetric physical equations shows mathematical interdependence between states without independently establishing a privileged direction in which earlier conditions causally force later choices.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins separates bidirectional mathematical recoverability from temporally privileged causal necessitation, using reversibility to expose equivocation between equations interrelating complete states and earlier conditions coercively producing deliberative outcomes. Principal limitation: Time symmetry removes an intrinsic temporal orientation yet remains compatible with laws and boundary conditions uniquely correlating every state, so rejecting forward-directed forcing does not establish alternative continuations, agent sourcehood, or indeterministic choice. Live burden: He must demonstrate why identical total physical conditions permit multiple genuinely available futures, or explain why libertarian responsibility needs sourcehood without branching, while distinguishing metaphysical possibility from unpredictability, ignorance, and reversible calculation. Locked score: Its central relevance and illuminating conceptual distinction therefore coexist with underqualified generalization, slightly overstated warrant, partly unstable scope, and an implicit bridge from nonprivileged causal direction to freedom.

con.words: Fixed physical conditions and laws can uniquely determine later states without causal necessitation, preserving determinist pressure against libertarian accounts that require genuinely branching continuations from one state.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley precisely grants the distinction between causal necessitation and mathematical determination, then shows that uniquely fixed continuations can still eliminate the branching alternatives targeted by libertarian freedom, making the reply direct, charitable, and burden-responsive. Principal limitation: Perfect predictability risks sounding epistemic unless grounded in ontological uniqueness, and the objection reaches only libertarian theories requiring multiple continuations from the same state and laws, not every sourcehood-centered account. Live burden: He must defend why fixed-law, fixed-state uniqueness obtains, and establish that Hawkins’s responsibility criterion requires objective branching instead of irreducible authorship compatible with a single continuation. Locked score: The explicit qualifications, stable terminology, coherent conditional structure, and decisive contact justify the very strong result, while comparatively thinner support for the uniqueness premise keeps evidential warrant below the reply’s outstanding responsiveness.

pro.words: Libertarian freedom combines agential sourcehood with relevant alternative possibilities, but those alternatives may obtain across suitably similar possible worlds without requiring an objectively branching future.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins confronts the branching-future objection by distinguishing agential sourcehood from objectively diverging actuality and locating alternative possibilities among relevantly comparable worlds, answering Folley’s deterministic pressure. Principal limitation: His comparability criterion remains insufficiently articulated, because leaving unspecified which circumstances, laws, reasons, and characteristics remain invariant risks manufacturing alternatives by modifying what explains the actual decision. Live burden: Hawkins must provide a principled similarity standard demonstrating that admissible counterfactual worlds preserve enough of the agent’s motivational and nomological situation to represent genuine ability rather than metaphysical redescription. Locked score: The strong/competent 75–84 band recognizes burden contact and intelligible sourcehood while withholding higher credit for unresolved modal constraints, unstable terminology, implicit qualification, and moderately secured warrant.

con.words: Possible worlds with altered pasts establish a broader ability than the consequence argument examines, because that narrower challenge asks what alternatives remain when actual history and laws stay fixed.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley differentiates unrestricted possible-world counterfactuality from the consequence argument’s fixed-history-and-laws accessibility relation, exposing why Hawkins’s sourcehood defense changes modal domains instead of answering the narrower alternatives challenge. Principal limitation: Although exceptionally explicit and charitable, the reply underdevelops the inference from fixed history and laws to inaccessible alternatives, leaving the consequence argument’s transfer principles undefended. Live burden: Hawkins must demonstrate that agential sourcehood supplies responsibility-relevant possibility while antecedent history and natural laws remain fixed, or explain why broader cross-world variation answers that constrained question. Locked score: This decisive, disciplined diagnostic reply merits the very strong 85–94 band because exceptional coherence, responsiveness, precision, and representational charity substantially outweigh its localized omission of a deeper consequence-argument defense.

pro.words: Causal determinism threatens rational normativity because merely caused beliefs and inferences may no longer answer to independent standards distinguishing correct reasoning from whatever thinking actually occurs.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins identifies a genuinely consequential distinction between norm-governed correctness and merely occurring cognition, then connects determinism’s credibility to whether rational endorsement can survive comprehensive causal explanation. Principal limitation: The argument moves from beliefs being causally produced to their being incapable of truth-sensitive, standards-responsive justification, without establishing that deterministic mechanisms cannot reliably instantiate logical sensitivity, evidential discrimination, or counterfactual responsiveness. Live burden: He must demonstrate an incompatibility between causal realization and normative answerability, addressing the determinist’s strongest charitable alternative that caused inferential processes can nevertheless track truth and adjust systematically to reasons. Locked score: The mixed result appropriately reflects a centrally relevant self-defeat challenge whose philosophical importance and clear burden contact exceed the developed support for its decisive bridging premise.

con.words: Non-causal determinism may strengthen compatibilism because complete predictability need not entail causal puppeteering, external compulsion, or the displacement of an agent's own deliberative processes.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley identifies a significant distinction between exhaustive predictability and causal puppeteering, opening a coherent compatibilist route that preserves deliberative agency without requiring indeterministic interruption or mysterious self-origination. Principal limitation: Removing causal compulsion does not independently establish authorship, reasons-responsiveness, alternative-sensitive control, or another positive condition sufficient for freedom, while the supposedly stronger status of non-causal determinism receives intuitive rather than discriminating argumentative support. Live burden: Folley must specify how non-causally determined deliberation belongs to the agent, explain why predictable decisions retain normatively relevant control, and distinguish this account from an equally predictable process that merely simulates autonomous evaluation. Locked score: The mixed evaluation appropriately recognizes a centrally relevant, cautiously calibrated conceptual opening while retaining substantial deductions for unstable terminology, compressed inferential bridging, and limited evidential development.

pro.words: Logical and mathematical relations establish standards independent of individual psychology, preserving an objective difference between valid inference and the patterns of thought people are causally disposed to follow.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins clearly separates psychologically prevalent reasoning from objectively correct inference, giving the pro case a positive account of logical success criteria instead of relying exclusively on a negative self-defeat objection. Principal limitation: The passage plausibly establishes standards independent of individual dispositions, yet it advances the stronger metaphysical conclusion that logical and mathematical relations are mind-independent without defending why intersubjective, constitutivist, or otherwise non-realist accounts cannot preserve normativity. Live burden: He must justify that transition from non-reducibility to actual psychology toward robust mind-independence, while explaining how abstract truth relations normatively govern concrete agents rather than merely describing valid formal relationships. Locked score: The strong result fits a precise, highly relevant constructive contribution, moderated by an evidential gap at the bounded bridge between objective correctness and the particular metaphysics asserted.

con.words: Freedom is functionally expressed through distinctions governing prediction, coercion, incentives, praise, and blame, all of which retain action-guiding significance within a deterministically organized society.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley offers a practical functional analysis, connecting freedom discourse to prediction, coercion-sensitive distinctions, incentives, praise, and blame, while showing why these practices remain intelligible and action-guiding in a deterministic society. Principal limitation: The argument moves too quickly from the functions of freedom concepts to freedom itself, because usefulness can explain why communities preserve responsibility language without demonstrating that agents possess authorship or control. Live burden: Folley must defend that constitutive bridge, distinguish legitimate responsibility from merely efficient behavioral management, and answer the libertarian who accepts those benefits while denying that functional success establishes sourcehood. Locked score: The strong evaluation fits the move’s exceptional burden relevance, concrete thought-experimental support, and disciplined plausibility claim, while preserving deductions for the unresolved function-to-constitution inference and incomplete comparison with rival accounts.

pro.words: Bradleyan idealism accepts scientific knowledge but denies its exhaustiveness, seeking a coherent metaphysics that integrates agency with moral, aesthetic, religious, felt, and scientific experience.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins clearly distinguishes accepting scientific truth from granting science exhaustive metaphysical authority, then specifies agential, moral, aesthetic, religious, and felt experience as domains any comprehensive worldview must coherently accommodate. Principal limitation: This breadth establishes an intelligible adequacy criterion but neither demonstrates that compatibilist pragmatism cannot recognize those domains as real nor establishes Bradleyan idealism as uniquely necessary for their integration. Live burden: He must directly confront the noncausal compatibilist basis, explain why practical freedom remains incomplete without idealist metaphysics, and derive that conclusion rather than relying upon science’s deliberate abstraction from evaluative experience. Locked score: The strong central relevance, explicit qualifications, stable scope, and recoverable proposition justify the competent assessment, while indirect responsiveness, underdeveloped alternatives, and only moderately secured warrant appropriately prevent a higher evaluation.

con.words: Experience-centered idealism can remain naturalistically acceptable when inquiry organizes experience and physical objects function as explanatory models, without positing mysterious mental substance or conscious control of reality.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley articulates a naturalistically respectable, experience-centered idealism that distinguishes methodological attention to experience from extravagant mental-substance ontology, while treating physical objects as explanatorily productive models rather than metaphysically exhaustive furniture. Principal limitation: The formulation leaves “idealism” oscillating between an epistemological orientation and an ontological commitment, and consequently underexplains whether experiential modeling can accommodate value, volition, normativity, and Hawkins’s non-intellectual feeling without redescribing or marginalizing them. Live burden: Folley must specify the metaphysical implications of experience-first inquiry and demonstrate that its naturalistic conceptual resources genuinely integrate those resistant dimensions, rather than merely permitting nonexhaustive science or declining mysterious substance. Locked score: This is a highly responsive, coherent central reply whose careful plausibility-level calibration and direct contact with both targeted claims outweigh its terminological instability and comparatively schematic warrant.

pro.words: Feeling and volition precede reflective systematization, while scientific inquiry deliberately abstracts from agential, ethical, and aesthetic value, indicating that intellectual description does not exhaust reality.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins identifies feeling, volition, ethical significance, aesthetic value, and pleasure as concrete dimensions that reflective intellectual systems may abstract from, thereby placing the idealist-completeness burden squarely at the exchange’s center. Principal limitation: The argument moves too quickly from methodological abstraction to metaphysical incompleteness, grouping several partly unstable concepts without showing that scientific naturalism categorically cannot investigate or accommodate agency and value. Live burden: He must distinguish precedence in experience from ontological priority, clarify the relationships among feeling, volition, and value, and establish why deliberate scientific selectivity supports idealism instead of merely describing specialized inquiry. Locked score: Exceptional relevance and concrete examples support the competent result, whereas the unsupported conditional, missing qualification, materially overstated necessity, and incomplete engagement with the methodological alternative appropriately constrain the evaluation.

sections.title: Idealist Truth, Feeling, and Perceptual Structure

pro.words: Bradleyan truth combines practical operation, felt encounter, and intellectual satisfaction, so judgment remains constrained by reality and false claims can fail rather than becoming true through voluntary choice.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins rejects voluntarist caricature by identifying three constraints—practical operation, felt encounter with reality, and intellectual satisfaction—while presenting Bradley's position as pragmatism supplemented by further requirements. Principal limitation: the reply enumerates constraints without validating them, because neither felt encounter nor intellectual satisfaction is sufficiently individuated as a truth-condition, and operational success could characterize coherent misconception. Live burden: Hawkins must explain how conceptually mediated feeling reliably discriminates reality-responsive judgment from durable error, especially when categorization structures reflective encounters and satisfaction may reward internal consistency rather than correspondence. Locked score: the engagement, qualification, and appeal to practical failure support the recorded assessment, while the unresolved epistemic-access difficulty and underdeveloped independence of the proposed constraints appropriately limit its evidential force.

con.words: Idealism need not imply voluntary control over experience, yet Bradley's inaccessible unstructured feeling faces epistemic pressure because reflective perception already presents experience through categories and distinctions.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley concedes that idealism does not entail voluntary control of reality, then isolates a precise epistemic difficulty: reflective perception arrives already categorized, whereas Bradley’s foundational felt real is characterized as antecedently unstructured. Principal limitation: The challenge rests on phenomenological assertion, without establishing that categorization conditions every evidential route or that reflective inaccessibility disqualifies a transcendental, rather than observational, foundation. Live burden: Folley must explain why structure in accessible perception undermines warranted inference to precognitive feeling, while Hawkins must identify a non-question-begging basis for attributing structurelessness and foundational significance to something unavailable as a reflective object. Locked score: The measured interrogative force, explicit concession, strong logical organization, and charitable targeting justify a strong assessment, although limited defense of universality and subsidiary burden contact constrain the result.

pro.words: Reflective agents never recover wholly unstructured experience, yet precognitive feeling remains thought's foundation and is ultimately integrated with thought and volition within the absolute.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins concedes that reflective judgment never recovers wholly unstructured experience, but distinguishes inaccessible precognitive feeling from its foundational role and integration with thought and volition in the absolute. Principal limitation: the explanation leaps from phenomenological inaccessibility to metaphysical indispensability, leaving “foundation,” “persistence,” and “integration” insufficiently stabilized, without independently warranting the posit beneath categorized experience. Live burden: Hawkins must show how an epistemically unavailable stratum is responsibly inferred, how it constrains conceptual judgment, and why absolute integration explains rather than abstractly redescribes Bradley's system. Locked score: the candid concession, central relevance, and accurate contact with the categorization objection justify the recorded strength, while the unsupported foundational inference and shifting explanatory scope properly restrain the evidential assessment.

sections.title: The Absolute, Inquiry, and Pragmatic Standards

pro.words: Inquiry's normative orientation toward fulfilled truth treats completed reality as more real than partial understanding, so the absolute functions as an existent completion rather than a convenient regulative fiction.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins confronts Folley’s regulative-fiction alternative, interpreting Bradley’s normative orientation toward consummated truth as ontological commitment relevant to the central realism burden. Principal limitation: The inference equivocates between evaluative superiority and metaphysical actuality: recognizing comprehensive understanding as normatively authoritative neither demonstrates an independently existent completion nor necessitates an already-real terminus. Live burden: Hawkins must justify why truth-directed aspiration metaphysically presupposes a completed whole, excluding the charitable possibility that regulative ideals guide indefinitely improvable inquiry without corresponding to any separately existing absolute. Locked score: The mixed 65–74 band appropriately recognizes direct, fully responsive burden contact and a recoverable Bradley-specific rationale, while substantially discounting materially overstated necessity, unstable “more real” terminology, unacknowledged modal uncertainty, and comparatively weak ontological warrant.

con.words: Bradley's absolute must be distinguished as either a regulative ideal guiding inquiry or an independently real completion whose asserted existence introduces an additional metaphysical commitment requiring justification.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley sharply distinguishes a merely regulative orientation for inquiry from an independently existent metaphysical completion, thereby locating the exact inferential transition Hawkins must justify. Principal limitation: The intervention remains interrogative and comparatively underdeveloped, supplying neither Bradley-specific textual evidence nor a sustained demonstration that epistemic directionality cannot warrant ontological actuality. Live burden: Hawkins must explain why convergence-oriented intelligibility authorizes realism about the absolute, while Folley must show that the regulative interpretation preserves Bradley's explanatory ambitions without covertly presupposing their metaphysical terminus. Locked score: The very strong 85–94 band is warranted because this charitable, precisely calibrated diagnostic exposes a central premise with exceptional relevance and coherence, yet its evidential development remains meaningfully thinner than its conceptual discrimination.

pro.words: Idealism makes inquiry intelligible by locating knower and known within an interactive experiential whole, so directed understanding can approach an attainable end rather than inaccessible independent reality.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Hawkins directly answers the regulative-or-real challenge by presenting inquiry as an experientially integrated relationship in which knower and known reciprocally interact, thereby explaining why understanding can intelligibly possess direction rather than confront an intrinsically inaccessible reality. Principal limitation: The argument insufficiently differentiates epistemic interaction, metaphysical unity, progressive intelligibility, and actual attainability, so movement toward improved understanding does not distinctively establish Bradleyan idealism or a completed absolute. Live burden: Hawkins must demonstrate why fallible pragmatic engagement with independently existing reality cannot supply comparable direction, and why reciprocal influence entails ontological inclusion instead of ordinary cognition. Locked score: The strong burden contact and highly responsive idealist explanation justify the recorded strong performance, while slightly overstated warrant, partly unstable terminology, and an underdeveloped inference from direction to terminus constrain its force.

con.words: Anti-reductionism needs pragmatic admission standards that avoid both scientistic exclusion and unrestricted metaphysical permissiveness, although selecting and operationalizing those standards remains genuinely difficult.
con.critique: Strongest feature: Folley charitably accepts the anti-reductionist motivation while identifying the decisive comparative problem: metaphysical inquiry needs discriminating admission standards that exclude neither legitimate nonscientific understanding nor intellectual discipline, and his tentative pragmatic maxim appropriately acknowledges uncertainty. Principal limitation: Although the proposal names both dangers, it does not operationalize pragmatic admissibility or explain which consequences distinguish a warranted substantive absolute from an imaginatively permissible construction. Live burden: Folley must specify assessable criteria, show how they adjudicate Bradleyan claims without covert scientism, and establish why normative direction supports only a regulative ideal rather than metaphysical completion. Locked score: The exceptionally direct burden contact, stable framing, explicit qualification, and charitable representation support the recorded very strong performance, while limited evidential development prevents the standard from becoming a decisive refutation.

strengths: Landed a clear distinction between actual psychological reasoning and objective logical standards, giving the normativity route concrete positive content.
Landed the important distinction between mathematical determination and temporally directed causal forcing, complicating simplistic deterministic imagery.
Landed an inclusive idealist program that accepts scientific truth while demanding integration of agency, feeling, morality, aesthetics, and religion.
Landed direct answers to voluntarist caricatures of idealism by identifying practical, felt, and intellectual constraints upon truth.
Landed substantial responsiveness throughout the absolute exchange by explaining how knower and known belong within an interactive experiential account.

blunders.text: The self-defeat argument treated causal production as threatening normative answerability without establishing why deterministic cognition cannot remain evidence-responsive and truth-sensitive.
The possible-world defense of alternative possibility did not specify which actual features must remain fixed, leaving it vulnerable to the fixed-past scope distinction.
The move from inquiry's normative direction to an independently real absolute exceeded the warrant supplied and left the regulative alternative insufficiently answered.

strengths: Landed the debate's sharpest modal distinction by separating broad possible-world variation from alternatives holding the actual past and laws fixed.
Landed a carefully qualified noncausal determinist challenge that preserved branching pressure without equating predictability with causal puppeteering.
Landed a concrete functional account connecting freedom discourse to coercion, prediction, incentives, praise, and blame under determinism.
Landed a naturalistically acceptable experience-first alternative that absorbed anti-exhaustion concerns without requiring mysterious mental substance.
Landed disciplined pressure on the absolute by distinguishing regulative guidance from independent reality and demanding pragmatic admission standards.

blunders.text: The initial noncausal compatibilist basis remained mostly negative, removing puppeteering imagery without yet supplying a developed positive condition for freedom.
The functional account did not fully bridge the gap between explaining what freedom practices accomplish and establishing what responsibility-bearing control consists in.
The proposed pragmatic admission standard remained underoperationalized, leaving unclear how it would adjudicate specific metaphysical claims rather than merely counsel restraint.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that libertarian idealism is strongest when sourcehood means norm-sensitive authorship within an experience-inclusive reality, without requiring crude temporal branching or scientific rejection.
premises: Rational agency involves constitutive standards: deliberation counts as reasoning only insofar as considerations can function for the agent as evidence, justification, and grounds for revision.
Causal realization alone does not destroy normativity; the sharper libertarian claim is that exhaustive determination may fail to explain an agent's authorship of norm-guided commitment.

Alternative possibility should be constrained by agentially relevant sameness, preserving the agent's reasons, character, capacities, and governing laws while allowing the exercise of evaluative attention to differ.
Scientific models may be fully true within their explanatory purposes while remaining nonexhaustive of first-person normativity, felt salience, value, and deliberative ownership.
The absolute is defensible only as a constrained metaphysical hypothesis whose value depends on integrating otherwise fragmented explanatory domains, not merely on inquiry having a direction.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore libertarian idealism remains a defensible comparative hypothesis if it explains norm-sensitive authorship and experiential integration better than its rivals, while treating modal alternatives and the absolute as constrained commitments requiring further defense.

newArguments.title: Attentional authorship
newArguments.text: A new defense can locate libertarian control in the agent's governance of attention rather than in an unexplained breach of physical law. Deliberation changes when an agent sustains, suppresses, or reorganizes which reasons become salient, and this organization can be assessed for fidelity to evidence and values. If no lower-level description explains why the person, as an integrated normative subject, owns that pattern of attention, sourcehood may remain explanatorily indispensable even where physical events are law-governed. This does not prove indeterminism; it identifies a specific phenomenon that a reductive account must explain.

newArguments.title: Integration as a test
newArguments.text: Idealist integration can be made discriminating by requiring cross-domain explanatory gains. A metaphysical proposal earns admission only if it clarifies why objective reasons can be personally motivating, why felt salience can disclose value without dictating truth, and why scientific abstractions remain reliable within limited purposes. The absolute then becomes a hypothesis evaluated by unification, constraint, and correction rather than an endpoint inferred from aspiration alone. This standard answers pragmatic pressure by exposing the proposal to comparative failure whenever a simpler naturalistic model integrates the same domains equally well.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that compatibilist pragmatism explains freedom through reasons-responsive control and socially embedded accountability while admitting experiential pluralism under disciplined, revisable standards.
premises: Deterministic pressure concerns whether the same complete past and laws permit another continuation, and broad modal variation cannot by itself answer that narrower question.
Freedom can consist in a control profile including sensitivity to reasons, absence of coercive bypass, stable evaluative capacities, and conduct attributable to the agent's deliberative organization.
Praise, blame, incentives, and prediction are justified only when they track that control profile, so practical usefulness does not by itself constitute or manufacture responsibility.

Naturalism can treat experience, value, and first-person deliberation as genuine explanatory subjects without claiming that current physical descriptions exhaust every legitimate level of understanding.

Metaphysical commitments should be admitted when they generate discriminating expectations, explanatory compression, or indispensable normative clarification, and should remain revisable when they fail those tests.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore compatibilist pragmatism can answer determinist and naturalist pressure if its responsibility practices track genuine reasons-responsive control and its pluralism admits experience without endorsing metaphysical commitments that add no discriminating explanation.

newArguments.title: Counterfactual guidance
newArguments.text: Compatibilist control can be tested through structured counterfactuals that do not require changing the actual past. Ask whether the agent's decision process would update under variations in available evidence, perceived reasons, coercive threats, or opportunities for reflection. These tests evaluate the internal organization of the mechanism rather than whether an identical total universe could branch. A process that systematically tracks reasons and corrects errors possesses a form of guidance control relevant to responsibility, whereas a bypassed, compulsive, or reasons-insensitive process does not. This creates a principled distinction beyond mere social convenience.

newArguments.title: A metaphysical budget
newArguments.text: Pragmatism can impose a metaphysical budget: every additional ontological commitment should purchase a specified explanatory gain that cannot be obtained through less demanding models. Experience, value, and inquiry remain admissible subjects because they organize observation, action, and correction; an independently real absolute requires a further demonstration that it improves prediction, unification, normative understanding, or error diagnosis. This budget does not prejudge unfamiliar metaphysics as false. It makes admission symmetrical and revisable, preventing both automatic scientistic exclusion and unrestricted acceptance while giving Bradleyan idealism a clear route to earn its stronger commitments.
